The scope-analysis fallback in _cte_reference_ids logs only the exception type at INFO, dropping message and traceback.
first_sql_keyword returns an empty string on TokenError with no log line, so a read-only-off read the tokenizer rejects loses its rows without trace.
The sqlglot>=30.22 floor is never tested; CI pins 30.25.0.
The mixed-case CTE name case is tested only on Postgres, not SQLite.
is_read_shaped docstring calls it a first-token check though the whole statement is tokenized; first_sql_keyword docstring attributes parenthesis skipping to the tokenizer.
tool-scratch-storage.md (and transport.md:125) define the result-table path without the tokenizer-rejection case and the read_result mark path.
TestSqliteRunnerCommentLedRowCap docstring records history rather than the guarded-against change.
tools.md says query_type is empty when no keyword leads, but first_sql_keyword returns a leading unquoted identifier uppercased.

## Code Review Findings
### 🟡 Suggestion / Minor (11)
<details><summary>11 items</summary>

1. `src/sqllens/agent/tools/run_sql.py` lines 73-78: `RunSqlTool` decides read versus write from two sources, its own dialect classifier and the runner's `read_result` frame mark. Only the factory wiring keeps the two in agreement. When the mark overrides the classifier, `metadata["query_type"]` can still report `""` or a non-read keyword, so the metadata contradicts the branch taken. No input reaches this through the shipped `build_agent` wiring. (raised by 1/6 agents)
2. `src/sqllens/safety/limits.py` lines 28-31: `READ_RESULT_ATTR` is a one-sided, string-keyed `df.attrs` mark. The runners' rows-affected frames carry no counterpart, and nothing in code makes a future runner decorator that rebuilds the frame keep the mark. (raised by 1/6 agents)
3. `src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py` lines 164-172: when identifier normalization or `traverse_scope` raises, the fallback logs only the exception type at INFO. It drops the message and traceback, so a programming error such as a renamed sqlglot attribute would silently turn CTE exclusion off with one terse log line. (raised by 1/6 agents)
4. `src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py` lines 70-71: `first_sql_keyword` returns `""` on a tokenizer `TokenError` with no log line. With read-only off, a read the engine runs but the tokenizer rejects (for example an unterminated trailing comment on SQLite) is reported as rows affected and its rows are dropped without trace. That routing is the behavior the criteria accept and a follow-up issue tracks; only the missing log is the finding. (raised by 1/6 agents)
5. `pyproject.toml` line 46: the new `sqlglot>=30.22` floor is never tested. CI pins sqlglot 30.25.0, so the MySQL carriage-return and nested-comment tests never run on 30.22, the release the floor depends on. (raised by 1/6 agents)
6. `tests/unit/test_safety.py` lines 975-998: the mixed-case CTE name case (`WITH PG_RECENT … FROM pg_recent`) is tested only on Postgres. No SQLite case checks that `normalize_identifiers` matches a CTE name regardless of letter case there. (raised by 1/6 agents)
7. `src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py` line 91: the `is_read_shaped` docstring calls it a "Cheap first-token check", but `first_sql_keyword` tokenizes the whole statement and a `TokenError` anywhere returns `""`. Line 49 also says opening parentheses are skipped by the tokenizer; the function's own loop skips them. (raised by 1/6 agents) <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=held limb-one=held limb-two=held; evidence: the finding disputes the docstring wording, not is_read_shaped's predicate; correcting it changes no output or branch. No .sh/.py/.jq/.yml reader or agent-instruction file reads this docstring; it is a source docstring never printed. -->
8. `docs/internal/agent/tool-scratch-storage.md` lines 7 and 14, and `docs/internal/mcp-server/transport.md` line 125: the definition of the result-table path leaves out that SQL the tokenizer rejects anywhere is not read-shaped, and that `RunSqlTool` also takes the table path for a frame carrying the `read_result` mark. (raised by 1/6 agents) <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=held limb-one=held limb-two=held; evidence: the finding disputes the doc text only; the routing in run_sql.py is unchanged by correcting it. git grep over .sh/.py/.jq/.yml/.toml, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, .claude/ and .prflow/skill-extensions/ found only code comments pointing at transport.md (sql_threads.py:41), no reader; internal docs are not published. -->
9. `tests/unit/test_safety_limits.py` lines 505-506: the `TestSqliteRunnerCommentLedRowCap` docstring records how the code used to behave rather than which wrong change the test guards against. (raised by 1/6 agents)
10. `docs/internal/mcp-server/tools.md` line 302: the doc says `query_type` is `""` when no keyword leads the statement. `first_sql_keyword` returns any leading unquoted identifier, uppercased (a pinned test gives `"FOO"` for `foo bar`), so the `""` rule is false for that input. (raised by 1/6 agents) <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=held limb-one=held limb-two=held; evidence: the finding disputes the doc sentence; first_sql_keyword's behavior is pinned by test_unquoted_identifier_is_returned and is unchanged by correcting the doc. git grep found _format.py:683 only pointing readers at tools.md, no tool or agent-instruction reader; internal doc, not published. -->
- VC-67: FAIL (suggestion) — The class docstring asserts `RunSqlTool` builds its result table for every statement `is_read_shaped` classifies as read-shaped, with the runner's dialect. [tests/unit/test_safety_limits.py:522]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  Docstring (tests/unit/test_safety_limits.py:522-523) says RunSqlTool builds its result table for every read-shaped statement, with the runner's dialect. In src/sqllens/agent/tools/run_sql.py:78-118, a read-shaped statement whose runner returns an empty frame (e.g. WITH w AS (... WHERE n > 99) SELECT n FROM w) takes the `df.empty` branch. That branch writes no file and builds a DataFrameComponent with rows=[] and columns=[], with text 'No rows returned'. It builds no result table. The dialect is also not the runner's: RunSqlTool takes its own `dialect` constructor arg (run_sql.py:29,47), and the tests pass it separately (test_safety_limits.py:553,584); factory.py:123 passes it from elsewhere. The wording is imprecise in two places: 'every' ignores the empty case, and 'the runner's dialect' misattributes where the dialect comes from. The non-empty case does build a table, and the tests only cover non-empty frames. This is a test docstring only, so the impact is small.

  </details>

</details>

checklist.evidence: Docstring (tests/unit/test_safety_limits.py:522-523) says RunSqlTool builds its result table for every read-shaped statement, with the runner's dialect. In src/sqllens/agent/tools/run_sql.py:78-118, a read-shaped statement whose runner returns an empty frame (e.g. WITH w AS (... WHERE n > 99) SELECT n FROM w) takes the `df.empty` branch. That branch writes no file and builds a DataFrameComponent with rows=[] and columns=[], with text 'No rows returned'. It builds no result table. The dialect is also not the runner's: RunSqlTool takes its own `dialect` constructor arg (run_sql.py:29,47), and the tests pass it separately (test_safety_limits.py:553,584); factory.py:123 passes it from elsewhere. The wording is imprecise in two places: 'every' ignores the empty case, and 'the runner's dialect' misattributes where the dialect comes from. The non-empty case does build a table, and the tests only cover non-empty frames. This is a test docstring only, so the impact is small.
